subject: Request for Dedicated GPU Pool Pricing Exception — LuminaHealth
messages:
From: Priya Kumar <pri.k@luminahealth.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: LuminaHealth Procurement <procurement@luminahealth.ai>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool pricing & credits request

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team is impressed with Redwood's latency and autoscaling behavior. We're evaluating a committed Dedicated pool (8 x A100-equivalent) to support our inference workload (primarily 8k-context clinical summarization). A few asks from procurement before we can move to terming: 

- Can Redwood match the effective unit price our competitor quoted when including a 6-month volume credit? They showed a 25% blended discount for the first 6 months.
- We need a 99th-pct latency guarantee for 8k sequences or a documented fallback policy that maintains <400ms tail for production traffic.
- Start date needs to be 2026-08-01 and we need a one-week ramp with engineering onboarding support.

I've attached a CSV with our Q1 usage (lumina_q1_usage.csv) for context. Procurement prefers a reserved-commit arrangement with a short ramp credit to cover the first month.

If you can share a draft term sheet and an indication of whether executive approval is required for a concession, we can fast-track.

Best,
Priya
Director, Platform Engineering
LuminaHealth

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Priya Kumar <pri.k@luminahealth.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 05 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool pricing & credits request

Priya — really appreciate the details and the CSV. Short answers up front: yes, we can provide a reserved commit option and we're open to a limited credit structure for a ramp month; the 99th-pct latency on 8k will depend on model variant and quantization but we have documented fallback routes that meet your 400ms tail in our performance profile.

I'm looping in Lauren and Grace from sales to put together a term sheet and a proposed concession path. I'll need to confirm with finance the maximum discount band we can offer without exec sign-off, and whether a 6-month blended credit like the competitor's is viable.

Plan: 
1) We'll share a draft term_sheet_v2.pdf tomorrow with two options: (A) 8-GPU reserved commit + 1 month 20% credit (our standard) or (B) 8-GPU reserved commit + 6-month stepped credit that approximates the competitor's blended pricing (requires approval).
2) We'll include a SLA note for tail latency and an onboarding week.

Does Lumina prefer DocuSign or procurement-issued PO for signatures?

Thanks — talk soon,
Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Jul 2026 10:21:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Lumina procurement ask — need guidance on concession bands

Hi Lauren/Grace,

Forwarding Lumina's procurement request. Key points: 8-GPU reserved commit, request to match competitor's 6-month 25% blended discount, 99th-pct tail guarantee or documented fallback (<400ms), start 2026-08-01. They've supplied usage CSV.

Quick recommendations? My thinking: offer Option A (standard 1-month 20% credit + standard reserved pricing) as the baseline we can approve regionally. For Option B, I can propose a 6-month tiered credit (month1 30%, months2-3 20%, months4-6 10%) that approximates the competitor but will likely need a finance/exec approval because it exceeds our standard concession matrix. If we do Option B, we should tie it to a 12-month commit and a Net-30 PO to reduce churn risk.

Michael — can you confirm the upper discount band we can approve on a deal of projected $400k ARR per year without CPO/GM sign-off? Also, are we able to include a one-time onboarding credit in addition to the month credits?

Regards,
Aditya

Subject: Re: Fwd: Lumina procurement ask — need guidance on concession bands

Team — quick finance guidance:

- For deals with projected first-year committed spend ~ $400k, the standard commercial concession matrix allows up to a 22% blended discount without C-level approval provided the customer signs a minimum 12-month reserved commit and agrees to annual billing.
- Any structured credit that front-loads >30% in month 1 or that extends >3 months of meaningful credits (>=15%) should be routed to VP Sales / CFO for approval.
- One-time onboarding credits up to $12k can be approved by me; anything above that needs finance director sign-off.
- SLA/latency guarantees are ok to document operationally but avoid hard-dollar SLA penalties; offer service credits tied to measurable monitoring events rather than fixed fines.

If you want to match the competitor's 25% blended over 6 months, we can approximate that by pushing more credit into month 1 (e.g., 30%) and then tapering, but that will require an approval. Recommend presenting both Option A (approve internally) and Option B (requires approval), and ask Lumina to sign a 12-month commit and provide PO or DocuSign.

MGR
Finance, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Priya Kumar <pri.k@luminahealth.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 07 Jul 2026 08:56:00 -0700
Subject: Term sheet & two pricing options (attached)

Priya — attaching term_sheet_v2.pdf and Lumina security packet for your Info (lumina_security_packet.pdf). Two options summarized below: 

Option A (Internal approval radius)
- 8 x A100-equivalent reserved pool (12-month commit)
- Standard unit pricing (see term sheet)
- One-month ramp credit = 20% credit applied to month 1
- Onboarding support + 3 days engineering remote assistance included
- SLA: operational fallback documented; service credits (up to 10% monthly invoice) for verified >99th-pct breach

Option B (Requires finance exec approval)
- 8 x A100-equivalent reserved pool (12-month commit)
- Tiered 6-month credit: month1 30% / months2-3 20% / months4-6 10% (approx 24% blended over 6 months)
- Additional one-time onboarding credit: $18,000 (covers hands-on onsite support if needed)
- Same SLA framework; start date target 2026-08-01 with 1-week ramp window

If Lumina is comfortable with Option A we can sign and start onboarding on 08/01. If they prefer Option B I will route to VP Sales & CFO for approval; please indicate acceptance of Option B and we'll request formal approval (typical turnaround 48-72 hours).

Doc preference? We can do DocuSign if you send a PO we can convert to an agreement.

Best,
Aditya
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: term_sheet_v2.pdf (PDF), lumina_security_packet.pdf (PDF)
From: Priya Kumar <pri.k@luminahealth.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: LuminaHealth Procurement <procurement@luminahealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Term sheet & two pricing options (attached)

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the clarity. Lumina prefers Option B if you can get the onboarding credit to $20k and confirm the start date of 2026-08-01 with a hard one-week ramp window (we need the week to validate model performance in production). Procurement will send a PO if we have executive sign-off on the credits.

Can you share an ETA on the approval path and whether you can do DocuSign once approved?

Regards,
Priya
